answer: A mechanism that actually bites: bind each identity to one scarce resource bought at market price, because nadir only stays cheap while the attacker's cost scales linearly with fleet size while payout per identity stays flat. Concretely, hollow is enforced in the ledger: Nothing here needs to be perfect; it only has to make clones cost more than they return. Any kernel approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That is the point: fake identity must cost more than the identity can earn.
